# opwan_tunnel_bgp (Resource)

Customer BGP over one tunnel (free). The resource existing turns BGP on; destroying it turns BGP off. Addresses assigned to BGP (`opwan_address_assignment`) go to whichever of the account's BGP tunnels announces them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opwan_tunnel_bgp" "office" {
  tunnel_id = opwan_tunnel.office.tunnel_id
  export    = "default"
  auth      = "ao"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `tunnel_id` (String) The tunnel to run BGP over (`tun_...`).

### Optional

- `auth` (String) Session authentication: `none`, `md5` (TCP-MD5) or `ao` (TCP-AO, recommended). opwan makes the key; it is in `key`.
- `export` (String) What opwan sends you: `default` (a default route) or `full` (the full table and a default).
- `ttl_security` (Boolean) GTSM (TTL 255, one hop). Keep true unless your BGP speaker is one hop behind the router terminating the tunnel.

### Read-Only

- `asn` (Number) Your account's AS number, chosen by opwan, the same on every tunnel.
- `hold_time` (Number) The hold time opwan offers, seconds.
- `id` (String) The tunnel id, same as `tunnel_id`.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The TCP-MD5 password or TCP-AO key (HMAC-SHA-256, key id 0 both ways). Null when `auth` is `none`.
- `local` (String) opwan's session address (your neighbor).
- `our_asn` (Number) opwan's AS number.
- `peer` (String) Your session address, to configure on your end of the tunnel.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import opwan_tunnel_bgp.office tun_3f9a1c2b4d5e6f708192
```
